claim: The kinesin-3 family member Unc-104/KIF1A is required for axonal transport of many presynaptic components to synapses.
source: The kinesin-3 family member Unc-104/KIF1A is required for axonal transport of many presynaptic components to synapses, and mutation of this gene results in synaptic dysfunction in mice, flies and worms.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about Unc-104/KIF1A function.

claim: Mutation of unc-104 results in synaptic dysfunction in mice, flies and worms.
source: The kinesin-3 family member Unc-104/KIF1A is required for axonal transport of many presynaptic components to synapses, and mutation of this gene results in synaptic dysfunction in mice, flies and worms.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about unc-104 mutations.

claim: Many synaptic defects in unc-104-null mutants are mediated independently of Unc-104's transport function.
source: Our studies at the Drosophila neuromuscular junction indicate that many synaptic defects in unc-104-null mutants are mediated independently of Unc-104's transport function, via the Wallenda (Wnd)/DLK MAP kinase axonal damage signaling pathway.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Synaptic defects in unc-104-null mutants are mediated via the Wallenda (Wnd)/DLK MAP kinase axonal damage signaling pathway.
source: Our studies at the Drosophila neuromuscular junction indicate that many synaptic defects in unc-104-null mutants are mediated independently of Unc-104's transport function, via the Wallenda (Wnd)/DLK MAP kinase axonal damage signaling pathway.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Wnd signaling becomes activated when Unc-104's function is disrupted.
source: Wnd signaling becomes activated when Unc-104's function is disrupted, and leads to impairment of synaptic structure and function by restraining the expression level of active zone (AZ) and synaptic vesicle (SV) components.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by puc-lacZ reporter data in Figure 4.

claim: Wnd signaling leads to impairment of synaptic structure and function by restraining the expression level of active zone (AZ) and synaptic vesicle (SV) components.
source: Wnd signaling becomes activated when Unc-104's function is disrupted, and leads to impairment of synaptic structure and function by restraining the expression level of active zone (AZ) and synaptic vesicle (SV) components.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 1, 2, 3, and 7.

claim: Wnd signaling suppresses the buildup of synaptic proteins in neuronal cell bodies.
source: This action concomitantly suppresses the buildup of synaptic proteins in neuronal cell bodies, hence may play an adaptive role to stresses that impair axonal transport.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 7 showing increased protein accumulation in cell bodies when wnd is mutated.

claim: Wnd signaling may play an adaptive role to stresses that impair axonal transport.
source: This action concomitantly suppresses the buildup of synaptic proteins in neuronal cell bodies, hence may play an adaptive role to stresses that impair axonal transport.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the abstract based on the observed function of Wnd in restraining protein expression.

claim: Wnd signaling becomes activated when pre-synaptic proteins are over-expressed.
source: Wnd signaling also becomes activated when pre-synaptic proteins are over-expressed, suggesting the existence of a feedback circuit to match synaptic protein levels to the transport capacity of the axon.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by puc-lacZ reporter data in Figure 8G.

claim: There exists a feedback circuit to match synaptic protein levels to the transport capacity of the axon.
source: Wnd signaling also becomes activated when pre-synaptic proteins are over-expressed, suggesting the existence of a feedback circuit to match synaptic protein levels to the transport capacity of the axon.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the abstract based on the observation that Wnd is activated by protein overexpression.

claim: In unc-104-null mutants, synaptic boutons fail to form.
source: At the Drosophila neuromuscular junction (NMJ), unc-104-null mutants are severely defective in the formation of presynaptic boutons, fail to localize SVs to NMJ terminals and show strong reductions in AZ localization (Pack-Chung et al., 2007 and Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1A and C.

claim: In unc-104-null mutants, SVs fail to localize to NMJ terminals.
source: At the Drosophila neuromuscular junction (NMJ), unc-104-null mutants are severely defective in the formation of presynaptic boutons, fail to localize SVs to NMJ terminals and show strong reductions in AZ localization (Pack-Chung et al., 2007 and Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1B and E.

claim: In unc-104-null mutants, there are strong reductions in AZ localization.
source: At the Drosophila neuromuscular junction (NMJ), unc-104-null mutants are severely defective in the formation of presynaptic boutons, fail to localize SVs to NMJ terminals and show strong reductions in AZ localization (Pack-Chung et al., 2007 and Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1A, D, and E.

claim: Disrupting wnd had no significant effect on bouton formation in single mutants.
source: We found that disrupting the axonal damage signaling kinase Wnd (wnd3 single mutants) had no significant effect on bouton formation, AZ number, or presynaptic protein localization, but double mutants with unc-104-null alleles (unc-104P350, unc-104170, and unc-10452), gave a very informative phenotype
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1C.

claim: Disrupting wnd had no significant effect on AZ number in single mutants.
source: We found that disrupting the axonal damage signaling kinase Wnd (wnd3 single mutants) had no significant effect on bouton formation, AZ number, or presynaptic protein localization, but double mutants with unc-104-null alleles (unc-104P350, unc-104170, and unc-10452), gave a very informative phenotype
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1D.

claim: Disrupting wnd had no significant effect on presynaptic protein localization in single mutants.
source: We found that disrupting the axonal damage signaling kinase Wnd (wnd3 single mutants) had no significant effect on bouton formation, AZ number, or presynaptic protein localization, but double mutants with unc-104-null alleles (unc-104P350, unc-104170, and unc-10452), gave a very informative phenotype
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1E.

claim: In unc-104null;wnd3/3 double mutants, synaptic bouton formation was restored to a wild type phenotype.
source: in unc-104null;wnd3/3 double mutants the synaptic bouton formation (Figure 1A and C), AZ number (Figure 1A and D), and synaptic levels of the AZ protein Brp (Figure 1A and E) were restored to a wild type phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1A and C.

claim: In unc-104null;wnd3/3 double mutants, AZ number was restored to a wild type phenotype.
source: in unc-104null;wnd3/3 double mutants the synaptic bouton formation (Figure 1A and C), AZ number (Figure 1A and D), and synaptic levels of the AZ protein Brp (Figure 1A and E) were restored to a wild type phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1A and D.

claim: In unc-104null;wnd3/3 double mutants, synaptic levels of the AZ protein Brp were restored to a wild type phenotype.
source: in unc-104null;wnd3/3 double mutants the synaptic bouton formation (Figure 1A and C), AZ number (Figure 1A and D), and synaptic levels of the AZ protein Brp (Figure 1A and E) were restored to a wild type phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1A and E.

claim: In unc-104null;wnd3/3 double mutants, the synaptic levels of SV proteins (VGlut, SytI and CSP) remained negligible.
source: In contrast, the synaptic levels of SV proteins (VGlut, SytI and CSP) remained negligible, as in the unc-104null single mutants (Figure 1B and E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1B and E.

claim: Unc-104 functions as an essential molecular motor to transport SV precursors to synaptic terminals.
source: These results are consistent with previous findings that Unc-104 functions as an essential molecular motor to transport SV precursors to synaptic terminals.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation consistent with the data showing persistent SV protein defects in double mutants.

claim: Transport of AZ precursors and bouton formation can occur independently of Unc-104.
source: However our findings indicate that transport of AZ precursors and bouton formation can occur independently of Unc-104.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the rescue of AZ and bouton defects in unc-104;wnd double mutants.

claim: AZ and bouton defects in unc-104 mutants are mediated by a mechanism that depends upon the function of the Wnd kinase.
source: These defects are mediated by a second and separable mechanism, which depends upon the function of the Wnd kinase.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the rescue data in Figure 1.

claim: In unc-104-hypomorph mutants, approximately 50% of PSDs lack apposing presynaptic AZ components.
source: All of these mutants share similar characteristics: Post Synaptic Densities (PSDs) form (identified by the presence of a core receptor subunit GluRIII), however ~50% lack apposing presynaptic AZ components, as identified by Brp (Figure 2A and C), Liprin-α (Figure 2B and D) and the voltage gated calcium channel Cac-GFP (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by quantification in Figure 2C and D.

claim: Mutations in wnd fully rescued presynaptic AZ assembly defects in unc-104-hypomorph mutants.
source: Similarly to the unc-104-null mutants (Figure 1), mutations in wnd fully rescued these presynaptic AZ assembly defects (Figure 2A–E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2A-E.

claim: RNAi knockdown of unc-104 using pan-motoneuron or single motoneuron driver lines led to AZ defects.
source: RNAi knockdown of unc-104 using either pan-motoneuron or single motoneuron driver lines led to AZ defects and concomitant knockdown of wnd in neurons led to rescue, (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), indicating a cell-autonomous role for both Unc-104 and Wnd in the synaptic defects.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Concomitant knockdown of wnd in neurons led to rescue of AZ defects caused by unc-104 knockdown.
source: RNAi knockdown of unc-104 using either pan-motoneuron or single motoneuron driver lines led to AZ defects and concomitant knockdown of wnd in neurons led to rescue, (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), indicating a cell-autonomous role for both Unc-104 and Wnd in the synaptic defects.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: There is a cell-autonomous role for both Unc-104 and Wnd in the synaptic defects.
source: RNAi knockdown of unc-104 using either pan-motoneuron or single motoneuron driver lines led to AZ defects and concomitant knockdown of wnd in neurons led to rescue, (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), indicating a cell-autonomous role for both Unc-104 and Wnd in the synaptic defects.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the RNAi rescue experiments.

claim: Inhibition of the downstream MAP Kinase JNK (Bsk) via expression of dominant-negative isoforms in neurons rescued the presynaptic defect in unc-104 single mutants.
source: We found that inhibition of the downstream MAP Kinase JNK (Bsk) and Fos transcription factor, via expression of dominant-negative (DN) isoforms in neurons, could also rescue the presynaptic defect shown in the unc-104 single mutants (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Inhibition of Fos transcription factor via expression of dominant-negative isoforms in neurons rescued the presynaptic defect in unc-104 single mutants.
source: We found that inhibition of the downstream MAP Kinase JNK (Bsk) and Fos transcription factor, via expression of dominant-negative (DN) isoforms in neurons, could also rescue the presynaptic defect shown in the unc-104 single mutants (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: A signaling pathway consisting of Wnd, JNK and Fos mediates synaptic defects observed in unc-104 mutants.
source: These results suggest that a signaling pathway consisting of Wnd, JNK and Fos mediates synaptic defects observed in unc-104 mutants.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the rescue experiments with wnd, bsk, and fos.

claim: Wnd pathway mutations caused a striking increase in quantity of VGlut at unc-104-hypomorphic mutant NMJs.
source: In contrast with unc-104-null mutants, we observed that wnd mutations caused a striking increase in quantity of VGlut at unc-104-hypomorphic mutant NMJs (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2F.

claim: Unc-104-hypomorph mutant NMJs have severely reduced mini frequency.
source: Unc-104-hypomorph mutant NMJs have severely reduced mini frequency, and modestly reduced mEJP amplitude, EJP amplitude and quantal content (Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to previous work.

claim: Unc-104-hypomorph mutant NMJs have modestly reduced mEJP amplitude.
source: Unc-104-hypomorph mutant NMJs have severely reduced mini frequency, and modestly reduced mEJP amplitude, EJP amplitude and quantal content (Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to previous work.

claim: Unc-104-hypomorph mutant NMJs have modestly reduced EJP amplitude.
source: Unc-104-hypomorph mutant NMJs have severely reduced mini frequency, and modestly reduced mEJP amplitude, EJP amplitude and quantal content (Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to previous work.

claim: Unc-104-hypomorph mutant NMJs have modestly reduced quantal content.
source: Unc-104-hypomorph mutant NMJs have severely reduced mini frequency, and modestly reduced mEJP amplitude, EJP amplitude and quantal content (Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to previous work.

claim: Mutations in wnd fully rescued the mEJP frequency defects in unc-104-hypomorph mutants.
source: We observed that mutations in wnd, jnk (bsk) or fos fully rescued the mEJP frequency defects (Figure 3A and C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3A and C.

claim: Mutations in jnk (bsk) fully rescued the mEJP frequency defects in unc-104-hypomorph mutants.
source: We observed that mutations in wnd, jnk (bsk) or fos fully rescued the mEJP frequency defects (Figure 3A and C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mutations in fos fully rescued the mEJP frequency defects in unc-104-hypomorph mutants.
source: We observed that mutations in wnd, jnk (bsk) or fos fully rescued the mEJP frequency defects (Figure 3A and C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: mEJP amplitude, EJP amplitude and quantal content were rescued by wnd mutations in unc-104-hypomorph mutants.
source: mEJP amplitude, EJP amplitude and quantal content were also rescued by wnd mutations (Figure 3), while Bsk (JNK) and Fos inhibition rescued some aspects of these defects (Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and Figure 3—source datas 1–3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: Bsk (JNK) and Fos inhibition rescued some aspects of mEJP amplitude, EJP amplitude and quantal content defects in unc-104-hypomorph mutants.
source: mEJP amplitude, EJP amplitude and quantal content were also rescued by wnd mutations (Figure 3), while Bsk (JNK) and Fos inhibition rescued some aspects of these defects (Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and Figure 3—source datas 1–3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Wnd pathway impairs multiple aspects of synaptic structure and transmission.
source: The suppression of these phenotypes by mutations in wnd suggests that the Wnd pathway impairs multiple aspects of synaptic structure and transmission.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the rescue data.

claim: The total levels of Unc-104 protein remained low in the unc-104hypomorph;wnd double mutants.
source: The total levels of Unc-104 protein remained low in the unc-104hypomorph;wnd double mutants (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Western blot data in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Defects in larval motility and lethality of unc-104-hypomorph mutants largely remained in unc-104hypomorph;wnd double mutants.
source: Moreover, defects in larval motility and lethality of unc-104-hypomorph mutants largely remained in unc-104hypomorph;wnd double mutants, implying the persistence of major defects from the loss of Unc-104's function (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: The extensive suppression of the synaptic defects at the larval NMJ is unlikely to be the result of increased stability of the residual Unc-104 protein.
source: Hence the extensive suppression of the synaptic defects at the larval NMJ is unlikely to be the result of increased stability of the residual Unc-104 protein.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation based on the persistence of Unc-104 protein deficiency and organismal defects.

claim: The synaptic phenotypes in unc-104 mutants reflect an activity of the Wnd pathway rather than a direct consequence of impaired Unc-104 driven transport.
source: Instead, as indicated by the suppression of unc-104-null defects (Figure 1), the synaptic phenotypes reflect an activity of the Wnd pathway rather than a direct consequence of impaired Unc-104 driven transport.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the rescue data.

claim: The basal expression of puc-lacZ is very low in wild type animals.
source: The basal expression of puc-lacZ is very low in wild type animals but was significantly increased in all unc-104 LOF mutant backgrounds (including bris/null, O3.1/null, and 2 independent RNAi lines) (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 4A and B.

claim: puc-lacZ expression was significantly increased in all unc-104 LOF mutant backgrounds.
source: The basal expression of puc-lacZ is very low in wild type animals but was significantly increased in all unc-104 LOF mutant backgrounds (including bris/null, O3.1/null, and 2 independent RNAi lines) (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 4A and B.

claim: The increase in puc-lacZ expression in unc-104 mutants was abolished when wnd was concomitantly knocked-down by RNAi.
source: This increase was abolished when wnd was concomitantly knocked-down by RNAi (Figure 4B), hence reflects activation of a Wnd-mediated nuclear signaling cascade.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 4B.

claim: The increase in puc-lacZ expression in unc-104 mutants reflects activation of a Wnd-mediated nuclear signaling cascade.
source: This increase was abolished when wnd was concomitantly knocked-down by RNAi (Figure 4B), hence reflects activation of a Wnd-mediated nuclear signaling cascade.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the puc-lacZ reporter data.

claim: Presynaptic nerve terminal morphology of unc-104 hypomorphic mutant NMJs show increased numbers of synaptic branches.
source: Additional evidence for Wnd signaling activation was revealed by the presynaptic nerve terminal morphology of unc-104 hypomorphic mutant NMJs, which show increased numbers of synaptic branches and boutons which are smaller in size ([Figure 4C and D], and Kern et al).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 4C and D.

claim: Presynaptic nerve terminal morphology of unc-104 hypomorphic mutant NMJs show boutons which are smaller in size.
source: Additional evidence for Wnd signaling activation was revealed by the presynaptic nerve terminal morphology of unc-104 hypomorphic mutant NMJs, which show increased numbers of synaptic branches and boutons which are smaller in size ([Figure 4C and D], and Kern et al).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 4C and D.

claim: Features of presynaptic nerve terminal overgrowth have previously been described for Wnd pathway activation.
source: These features of presynaptic nerve terminal overgrowth have previously been described for Wnd pathway activation (Brace et al., 2014; Collins et al., 2006; Valakh et al., 2013; Wu et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to previous work.

claim: The overgrowth phenotype in unc-104 mutants requires the function of Wnd, JNK and Fos in presynaptic motoneurons.
source: We confirmed that this overgrowth phenotype in unc-104 mutants requires the function of Wnd, JNK and Fos in presynaptic motoneurons (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 4C and D.

claim: unc-104-hypomorph mutants showed an enhanced ability to regrow axons after injury.
source: Finally, we observed that unc-104-hypomorph mutants showed an enhanced ability to regrow axons after injury (Figure 4E–G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 4E-G.

claim: Activation of Wnd/DLK signaling enhances the ability of axons to initiate regenerative axonal growth after injury.
source: Since previous studies have shown that activation of Wnd/DLK signaling enhances the ability of axons to initiate regenerative axonal growth after injury (Hammarlund et al., 2009; Shin et al., 2012; Xiong et al., 2010; Yan et al., 2009), the activation of Wnd signaling in unc-104 mutants may explain this kinesin's paradoxical function in restraining rather than promoting axonal growth.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to previous work.

claim: The activation of Wnd signaling in unc-104 mutants may explain this kinesin's paradoxical function in restraining rather than promoting axonal growth.
source: Since previous studies have shown that activation of Wnd/DLK signaling enhances the ability of axons to initiate regenerative axonal growth after injury (Hammarlund et al., 2009; Shin et al., 2012; Xiong et al., 2010; Yan et al., 2009), the activation of Wnd signaling in unc-104 mutants may explain this kinesin's paradoxical function in restraining rather than promoting axonal growth.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation connecting Wnd activation to axonal growth phenotypes.

claim: Mutations which inhibit kinesin-1, dynein and dynactin did not significantly affect the expression of puc-lacZ.
source: Previous studies have suggested links between JNK signaling and the regulation of axonal transport (Fu and Holzbaur, 2014; Verhey and Hammond, 2009). It is therefore interesting that other mutations that disrupt axonal transport, including mutations which inhibit kinesin-1, dynein and dynactin, did not significantly affect the expression of puc-lacZ (Figure 4B and Xiong et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 4B.

claim: There is a unique functional interdependence between Wnd pathway and the Unc-104 kinesin.
source: Altogether, our results suggest a unique functional interdependence between Wnd pathway and the Unc-104 kinesin, and that the Wnd signaling pathway becomes activated when Unc-104's function is lost.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the specificity of Wnd activation to unc-104 mutations.

claim: The protein levels of Wnd and its DLK homologues in mammals and C. elegans are strictly regulated.
source: Previous studies have established that the protein levels of Wnd and its DLK homologues in mammals and C. elegans are strictly regulated, and positively correlate with the activity of Wnd signaling pathway (Feoktistov and Herman, 2016; Hao et al., 2016; Huntwork-Rodriguez et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to previous work.

claim: Wnd/DLK protein levels positively correlate with the activity of Wnd signaling pathway.
source: Previous studies have established that the protein levels of Wnd and its DLK homologues in mammals and C. elegans are strictly regulated, and positively correlate with the activity of Wnd signaling pathway (Feoktistov and Herman, 2016; Hao et al., 2016; Huntwork-Rodriguez et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to previous work.

claim: A highly conserved ubiquitin ligase domain protein Hiw/Rpm-1/Phr1 restricts the levels of Wnd/DLK protein.
source: A highly conserved ubiquitin ligase domain protein Hiw/Rpm-1/Phr1 restricts the levels of Wnd/DLK protein and inhibits Wnd/DLK signaling activation in wild type animals (Babetto et al., 2013; Collins et al., 2006; Nakata et al., 2005; Xiong et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to previous work.

claim: Hiw/Rpm-1/Phr1 inhibits Wnd/DLK signaling activation in wild type animals.
source: A highly conserved ubiquitin ligase domain protein Hiw/Rpm-1/Phr1 restricts the levels of Wnd/DLK protein and inhibits Wnd/DLK signaling activation in wild type animals (Babetto et al., 2013; Collins et al., 2006; Nakata et al., 2005; Xiong et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to previous work.

claim: Mutations in hiw lead to strongly elevated levels of Wnd protein whose localization can be detected in neurites and at synapses.
source: Mutations in hiw lead to strongly elevated levels of Wnd protein whose localization can be detected in neurites and at synapses (Collins et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to previous work.

claim: Mutations in unc-104 did not lead to a detectable increase in global levels of endogenous Wnd protein by Western Blot.
source: In contrast to hiw, mutations in unc-104 did not lead to a detectable increase in global levels of endogenous Wnd protein by Western Blot (Figure 5A), or in synaptic Wnd protein level (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Western blot data in Figure 5A.

claim: Mutations in unc-104 did not lead to a detectable increase in synaptic Wnd protein level.
source: In contrast to hiw, mutations in unc-104 did not lead to a detectable increase in global levels of endogenous Wnd protein by Western Blot (Figure 5A), or in synaptic Wnd protein level (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by imaging data in Figure 5B.

claim: unc-104 mutants do not share the previously reported phenotype of hiw mutants of delayed axonal degeneration.
source: In addition, unc-104 mutants do not share the previously reported phenotype of hiw mutants of delayed axonal degeneration (Xiong et al., 2012, and data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to previous work.

claim: The mechanism of Wnd signaling activation in unc-104 mutants is unlikely to occur via Hiw.
source: These observations suggest that the mechanism of Wnd signaling activation in unc-104 mutants is unlikely to occur via Hiw.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the differences between unc-104 and hiw mutants.

claim: MiMIC-wnd-GFP revealed Wnd enrichment in neuronal cell bodies in unc-104 mutants.
source: By IHC, this reagent revealed Wnd enrichment in neuronal cell bodies in unc-104 mutants (Figure 5C and E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by imaging data in Figure 5C and E.

claim: Ectopically expressed UAS-GFP-wndKD transgene revealed an increase in cell body localized Wnd in unc-104 mutants.
source: Second, an ectopically expressed UAS-GFP-wndKD transgene (which was kinase dead to avoid pathway activation) has been established as a sensitive method to detect Wnd protein change (Collins et al., 2006; Hao et al., 2016; Xiong et al., 2010). This highly expressed transgene also revealed an increase in cell body localized Wnd in unc-104 mutants (Figure 5D and F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by imaging data in Figure 5D and F.

claim: Wnd and its DLK homologue physically associate with vesicles that are transported in axons.
source: This correlation of Wnd localization with signaling activation is interesting to note, since Wnd and its DLK homologue are known to physically associate with vesicles that are transported in axons (Holland et al., 2016; Xiong et al., 2010), and this transport appears to be important for its ability to mediate axon-to-cell body retrograde signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to previous work.

claim: Transport of Wnd-associated vesicles appears to be important for Wnd's ability to mediate axon-to-cell body retrograde signaling.
source: This correlation of Wnd localization with signaling activation is interesting to note, since Wnd and its DLK homologue are known to physically associate with vesicles that are transported in axons (Holland et al., 2016; Xiong et al., 2010), and this transport appears to be important for its ability to mediate axon-to-cell body retrograde signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to previous work.

claim: Live imaging analysis of UAS-GFP-wndKD vesicles showed no impairment in transport kinetics or flux in unc-104 mutants.
source: From live imaging analysis of UAS- GFP-wndKD vesicles we observed no impairment in transport kinetics or flux in unc-104 mutants (Figure 5—figure supplement 2), and no co-localization for Wnd and Unc-104 (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: There was no co-localization for Wnd and Unc-104.
source: From live imaging analysis of UAS- GFP-wndKD vesicles we observed no impairment in transport kinetics or flux in unc-104 mutants (Figure 5—figure supplement 2), and no co-localization for Wnd and Unc-104 (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: There is no evidence for Wnd as a direct cargo of Unc-104.
source: Therefore we found no evidence for Wnd as a direct cargo of Unc-104.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the transport and colocalization data.

claim: Liprin-α, Rab3 and Rab3-GEF play important early roles in AZ assembly.
source: We then considered the possibility that Unc-104 regulates Wnd signaling indirectly via the transport of another cargo. Previous work has suggested that other presumed cargo of Unc-104, including Liprin-α, Rab3 and Rab3-GEF, play important early roles in AZ assembly (Graf et al., 2009; Niwa et al., 2008; Shin et al., 2003; Südhof, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to previous work.

claim: liprin-α mutant NMJs contain a large portion of unapposed GluRIII-labeled PSDs.
source: We observed that liprin-α mutant NMJs contain a large portion of unapposed GluRIII-labeled PSDs (Figure 5G), resembling the defects in unc-104 mutants.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by imaging data in Figure 5G.

claim: Similar defects to liprin-α mutants were reported for rab3 and rab3-gef mutants.
source: Similar defects were reported for rab3 and rab3-gef mutants (Bae et al., 2016; Graf et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to previous work.

claim: The liprin-α and rab3 synaptic defects were not suppressed by mutations in wnd.
source: However, in contrast to unc-104, the liprin-α and rab3 synaptic defects were not suppressed by mutations in wnd (Figure 5G–I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5G-I.

claim: The increased Brp intensity per AZ and reduced AZ number due to liprin-α and rab3 mutations was not suppressed by wnd mutations.
source: Furthermore, the increased Brp intensity per AZ and reduced AZ number due to liprin-α and rab3 mutations was not suppressed by wnd mutations (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: The Brp intensity per AZ was slightly enhanced in liprin-α;wnd double mutants.
source: In fact, the Brp intensity per AZ was slightly enhanced in liprin-α;wnd double mutants.

claim: Liprin-α and Rab3 regulate presynaptic assembly via pathways that are either independent or downstream of Wnd.

claim: Defects in synapse assembly and structure per se do not cause activation of Wnd signaling.
source: These data suggest that Liprin-α and Rab3 regulate presynaptic assembly via pathways that are either independent or downstream of Wnd, and that defects in synapse assembly and structure per se do not cause activation of Wnd signaling.

evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 6B.

claim: Over-expression of wnd in motoneurons resulted in a global 70% reduction in Brp intensity across the entire NMJ terminal.
source: First, many individual synapses (identified by GluRIII puncta) lacked Brp (Figure 6A and C), and synapses that contained Brp had reduced Brp intensity, which resulted in a global 70% reduction in Brp intensity across the entire NMJ terminal (Figure 6B).

source: Second, mEJP frequency, along with other aspects of synaptic transmission (amplitude of EJP and mEJP), was significantly impaired (Figure 6D–I).

claim: Activation of the Wnd signaling pathway leads to strong perturbations in presynaptic structure and function.
source: Taken together with the rescue of unc-104 synaptic defects by wnd mutations (Figures 1–3), these data indicate that activation of Wnd signaling leads to strong perturbations in presynaptic structure and function.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the wnd overexpression and rescue data.

claim: hiw mutants displayed strikingly similar presynaptic defects to unc-104 mutants or overexpression of Wnd.
source: As noted above, Wnd signaling also becomes activated when an upstream negative regulator, Hiw, is mutated (Collins et al., 2006; Nakata et al., 2005). We found that hiw mutants displayed strikingly similar presynaptic defects to unc-104 mutants or overexpression of Wnd (Figure 6—figure supplements 1 and 2).

claim: In hiw mutants, 60% of synapses lacked the AZ proteins Brp, Liprin-α and Cac.
source: These included 60% of synapses lacking the AZ proteins Brp, Liprin-α and Cac (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B and E), a reduction of total Brp intensity at individual synapses and across the NMJ terminal (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C–D), a reduction in VGlut intensity at the NMJ terminal (Collins et al., 2006), and reduced mEJP frequency (Collins et al., 2006) and Figure 6—figure supplement 2).

claim: In hiw mutants, there is a reduction of total Brp intensity at individual synapses and across the NMJ terminal.
source: These included 60% of synapses lacking the AZ proteins Brp, Liprin-α and Cac (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B and E), a reduction of total Brp intensity at individual synapses and across the NMJ terminal (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C–D), a reduction in VGlut intensity at the NMJ terminal (Collins et al., 2006), and reduced mEJP frequency (Collins et al., 2006) and Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C-D.

claim: In hiw mutants, there is a reduction in VGlut intensity at the NMJ terminal.

evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to previous work.

claim: In hiw mutants, there is reduced mEJP frequency.

claim: All presynaptic defects in hiw mutants were rescued by wnd mutations.
source: All these presynaptic defects were rescued by wnd mutations.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 6—figure supplements 1 and 2.

claim: A previously described Wnd-independent defect in quantal content remains in hiw;wnd double mutants.
source: Meanwhile, a previously described Wnd-independent defect in quantal content remains in hiw;wnd double mutants (Figure 6—figure supplement 2, and Collins et al., 2006).

claim: Activation of the Wnd signaling pathway in multiple scenarios all lead to a shared set of characteristic defects in presynaptic structure and synaptic transmission.
source: Taken together, these observations indicate that activation of the Wnd signaling pathway in multiple scenarios—in unc-104 mutants, in hiw mutants, or when Wnd is ectopically over-expressed—all lead to a shared set of characteristic defects in presynaptic structure and synaptic transmission.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data from multiple genetic manipulations.

claim: One of the hallmarks of the unc-104 mutant phenotypes is the aggregation of protein components of both SVs and AZs in neuronal cell bodies.
source: One of the hallmarks of the unc-104 mutant phenotypes is the aggregation of protein components of both SVs and AZs in neuronal cell bodies (Hall and Hedgecock, 1991; Pack-Chung et al., 2007).

claim: wnd mutations enhanced the aggregation of SV and AZ components in cell bodies of unc-104 mutants.
source: Strikingly, wnd mutations enhanced this phenotype: SV and AZ components were dramatically increased in cell bodies of unc-104; wnd double mutants (Figure 7A,C,E, and Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 7A, C, E, and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: A similar increase in cell body protein accumulation was observed when either bsk or fos was inhibited in the unc-104 mutant background.
source: We observed a similar increase when either bsk or fos was inhibited in the unc-104 mutant background (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: The total levels of Brp and VGlut are reduced by 65% and 80% respectively in unc-104 mutants compared with wildtype animals.
source: We found that compared with wildtype animals, the total levels of Brp and VGlut are reduced by 65% and 80% respectively in unc-104 mutants (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by quantification in Figure 7F.

claim: The total levels of both Brp and VGlut were restored in unc-104; wnd double mutants.
source: The total levels of both proteins were restored in unc-104; wnd double mutants, with increases observed in all of the compartments (cell bodies, axons, and synapses). (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by quantification in Figure 7F.

claim: Increases in Brp and VGlut were observed in all compartments (cell bodies, axons, and synapses) in unc-104; wnd double mutants.
source: The total levels of both proteins were restored in unc-104; wnd double mutants, with increases observed in all of the compartments (cell bodies, axons, and synapses). (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by quantification in Figure 7F.

claim: Activated Wnd signaling leads to a down-regulation of the expression levels of multiple pre-synaptic proteins in unc-104 mutants.
source: These observations, combined with the observations that Wnd activation reduces the levels of Brp and VGlut at NMJs, suggest a model in which activated Wnd signaling leads to a down-regulation of the expression levels of multiple pre-synaptic proteins in unc-104 mutants.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the protein level data.

claim: Wnd signaling may serve to counteract presynaptic protein buildup in neuronal cell bodies while causing defects in synapse structure and function.
source: This response may serve to counteract their buildup in neuronal cell bodies while causing the observed defects in synapse structure and function.

claim: unc-104 mutations led to decreased expression of a vglut-DsRed transcriptional reporter in motoneurons, in a Wnd-dependent manner.

claim: Wnd signaling may inhibit presynaptic protein expression at the transcriptional level.
source: This, together with the involvement of transcription factor Fos in restraining VGlut and Brp buildup in cell bodies (Figure 7—figure supplement 2), implies that Wnd signaling may inhibit presynaptic protein expression at the transcriptional level.

claim: wnd mutants showed a premature onset of SV protein expression during embryonic stages of axonal outgrowth and synapse formation.
source: However, wnd mutants showed a premature onset of SV protein expression (Figure 8).

claim: In wild type embryos VGlut protein expression was undetectable until late embryonic stage 15.
source: In wild type embryos VGlut protein expression was undetectable until late embryonic stage 15, which coincides with the time at which motoneuron axons first reach their target muscles (Johansen et al., 1989).

claim: VGlut first appears in cell bodies at embryonic stage 15 and then becomes detectable at synapses at stage 16 and beyond.
source: VGlut first appears in cell bodies (Figure 8A–C) and then becomes detectable at synapses at stage 16 and beyond (Figure 8D), consistent with continued expression and transport to synaptic terminals as the NMJ terminal expands.

claim: In wnd mutants VGlut expression levels resemble wild type at stage 16 and beyond.
source: In wnd mutants VGlut expression levels resemble wild type at stage 16 and beyond, however its initial expression in cell bodies became apparent at an earlier time point, in early embryonic stage 15 (Figure 8B–C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 8B-C.

claim: In wnd mutants, VGlut initial expression in cell bodies became apparent at an earlier time point, in early embryonic stage 15.
source: In wnd mutants VGlut expression levels resemble wild type at stage 16 and beyond, however its initial expression in cell bodies became apparent at an earlier time point, in early embryonic stage 15 (Figure 8B–C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 8B-C.

claim: SytI intensity was increased in wnd mutants at early embryonic stage 16.

claim: Endogenous Wnd signaling may function in pacing the onset of expression of SV proteins.

claim: Pan-neuronal overexpression of SytI caused a significant induction of the Wnd responsive puc-lacZ reporter.

evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 8G.

claim: Pan-neuronal overexpression of VGlut caused a significant induction of the Wnd responsive puc-lacZ reporter.
source: To test this, we individually overexpressed three different components pan-neuronally: Brp, SytI and VGlut. Each caused a significant induction of the Wnd responsive puc-lacZ reporter (Figure 8G).

claim: Wnd signaling is sensitive to accumulations of presynaptic proteins in cell bodies.
source: These results, taken together with the cell autonomous nature of Wnd activation in unc-104 mutants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), suggest that Wnd signaling is sensitive to accumulations of presynaptic proteins in cell bodies.

claim: Major aspects of synaptic defects in unc-104 mutants, including impaired AZ addition and development of synaptic boutons, are not mediated by a direct transport role for the Unc-104 protein.

evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a primary conclusion of the study.

claim: Transport of SV precursors to synaptic terminals is likely a direct function of Unc-104.

source: Rather, the unc-104null;wnd double mutants reveal separable functions for Unc-104: (1) Transport of SV precursors to synaptic terminals is likely a direct function, since the failure to deliver adequate VGlut, Syt1 and CSP persists in unc-104null;wnd double mutants, and the Unc-104 homologue KIF1A physically interacts with SV precursors (Okada et al., 1995).

claim: The Wnd/DLK signaling pathway may contribute to impaired dendritic branching in unc-104 mutants.
source: With the knowledge that the Wnd/DLK signaling pathway is activated in unc-104 mutants, it is now worth considering whether it contributes to other phenotypes previously described for Unc-104 and its homologues in other species. These include impaired dendritic branching (Kern et al., 2013), increased microtubule dynamics (Chen et al., 2012), and failed neuronal remodeling (Park et al., 2011). It now becomes likely that these defects are mediated by Wnd/DLK, since Wnd/DLK signaling has previously been shown to influence microtubule growth (Hirai et al., 2011; Lewcock et al., 2007), neuronal remodeling (Kurup et al., 2015; Marcette et al., 2014) and dendrite growth (Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as speculation based on known functions of Wnd/DLK.

claim: DLK activation may mediate deleterious aspects of disease pathologies associated with human mutations in KIF1A.
source: Human mutations in KIF1A have been associated with hereditary spastic paraplegia (SPG30) (Fink, 2013), and hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type IIC (HSN2C) (Rivière et al., 2011). The possibility that DLK activation mediates deleterious aspects of these disease pathologies becomes an interesting future question.

claim: Disruption of Unc-104 mediated transport, potentially via mislocalization of Unc-104's cargo, may mediate Wnd/DLK's activation after cytoskeletal disruption and potentially after axonal injury.
source: This specificity suggests that disruption of Unc-104 mediated transport, potentially via mislocalization of Unc-104's cargo, mediates Wnd/DLK's activation after cytoskeletal disruption and potentially after axonal injury.

claim: Wnd signaling is sensitive to mislocalized presynaptic proteins as a feature of aberrant cargo transport.
source: These observations suggest a model that accumulations of presynaptic proteins, as a feature of aberrant cargo transport, are 'sensed' by Wnd signaling (Figure 9).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a proposed model based on the data.

claim: Wnd signaling restrains the expression of a cohort of presynaptic proteins.
source: In addition to VGlut, SytI, CSP-1, Brp, Liprin-α and Cac, we suspect that Wnd signaling restrains the expression of a cohort of presynaptic proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the observed effects on multiple proteins.

claim: Regulation of multiple targets required for synapse development and maintenance can explain the severe defects in unc-104-hypomorph mutants.
source: Regulation of multiple targets required for synapse development and maintenance can explain the severe defects in unc-104-hypomorph mutants, and the dramatic suppression by disruption of the Wnd pathway (Figures 2 and 3).

claim: Presynaptic defects in unc-104-hypomorph mutants can be partially rescued by overexpressing Brp.
source: In support of this idea, presynaptic defects in unc-104-hypomorph mutants can be partially rescued by overexpressing Brp (Kern et al., 2013) or Rab3 (Zhang et al., 2016).

claim: Presynaptic defects in unc-104-hypomorph mutants can be partially rescued by overexpressing Rab3.
source: In support of this idea, presynaptic defects in unc-104-hypomorph mutants can be partially rescued by overexpressing Brp (Kern et al., 2013) or Rab3 (Zhang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to previous work.

claim: The targets of Wnd regulation are abundant presynaptic proteins and are thought to be major cargo for axonal transport.
source: It is interesting to consider that the targets of Wnd regulation are also abundant presynaptic proteins, and are thought to be major cargo for axonal transport (Figure 9).

claim: Down-regulation of presynaptic proteins in response to defects in their transport or after axonal damage may comprise a stress response mechanism to prevent unwanted buildup or wasted cellular resources.
source: Down-regulation of these proteins in response to defects in their transport or after axonal damage may comprise a stress response mechanism to prevent unwanted buildup or wasted cellular resources.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the adaptive function of Wnd signaling.

claim: Additional post-transcriptional mechanisms, such as regulation of protein stability or translation, or bulk turnover via autophagy, may factor into the regulation of presynaptic proteins by Wnd.
source: It is also possible that additional post-transcriptional mechanisms, such as regulation of protein stability or translation, or bulk turnover via autophagy, factor into the regulation of presynaptic proteins by Wnd.

claim: DLK may activate the integrated stress response pathway in mammalian neurons.

claim: JNK signaling may directly regulate the function of kinesin-1, modulating its cargo binding, affinity for microtubules and its processivity.
source: Many previous studies have reported links between JNK signaling and kinesin-driven transport (Verhey and Hammond, 2009), with some observations suggesting that JNK signaling may directly regulate the function of kinesin-1, modulating its cargo binding, affinity for microtubules and its processivity (Fu and Holzbaur, 2013; Horiuchi et al., 2007; Morfini et al., 2006; Stagi et al., 2006; Sun et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to previous work.

claim: A commonly described defect in axonal transport mutants is the presence of accumulations of cargo within axons, referred to as 'traffic jams'.
source: A commonly described defect is the presence of accumulations of cargo within axons, referred to as 'traffic jams'. These defects have been noted for many different mutations, including kinesin-1 and dynein subunits (Gindhart et al., 1998; Hurd and Saxton, 1996; Martin et al., 1999), and also in mutants for wnd and other members of JNK signaling pathways (Bowman et al., 2000; Horiuchi et al., 2005, 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to previous work.

claim: unc-104 mutations do not cause 'traffic jams' in axons, but instead leads to accumulations of synaptic proteins in cell bodies.
source: Intriguingly, unc-104 mutations do not cause this type of 'traffic jams' in axons, but instead leads to accumulations of synaptic proteins in cell bodies, which correlates with the activation of Wnd signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an observation distinguishing unc-104 from other transport mutants.

claim: Regulation of presynaptic proteins by Wnd may comprise a first order response that may facilitate adaptation to stress.

evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as speculation about the hierarchy of stress responses.

claim: Cell death could be the consequence when compensatory mechanisms fail in response to stress.
source: In analogy with other stress response pathways, regulation of presynaptic proteins may comprise a first order response that may facilitate adaptation to stress, while cell death could be the consequence when compensatory mechanisms fail.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as speculation about the hierarchy of stress responses.

claim: Inhibition of synaptic proteins is a pathology that becomes relevant for long term maintenance of synapses and their function over time.
